idea.title: A small avatar can make a carousel footer feel personal without changing the content
idea.summary: A carousel branding pass kept the existing username and slide copy intact, replacing only an initials mark with the portfolio profile image in the footer.

context.goal: Match the reference carousel's header and footer treatment without changing its text.
context.situation: The renderer's personal carousel frame had a header label, slide counter, and a branded footer using initials beside the existing username.
context.decision: Reuse the existing profile image from the portfolio build and serve a copy through the renderer's workspace static-asset directory.
context.implementation: Replaced the initials mark with a compact circular image using cover cropping; retained the existing footer username and all carousel content.
context.result: The profile image and active carousel were both served locally, and the renderer type-check, build, adapter tests, and whitespace check passed.

learning_points: A visual branding update can stay narrowly scoped when text and content contracts are left untouched.
A renderer's existing static-asset path is sufficient for a reusable local profile image; no new asset pipeline is required.
story_points: The placeholder initials already fit the footer geometry, so only the visual asset needed replacement.
The provided image was verified before it was added to the carousel workspace.
possible_angles: How to make reusable carousel branding feel personal without rewriting the post.
Why a small, scoped visual change is often better than a redesign.

notes: No render screenshot was captured because this session had no available browser surface.
